text:
maria: heads-up, northstar region just got an unexpected traffic reroute from CDN — GPU queues 4x baseline and p50 token latency climbing fast. seeing queue lengths ~1800 across the cluster.
lee: link to the dashboard? which pools are hot?
maria: https://dash.internal/redwood/northstar/admit — `pool:gpu-v100-4` mostly, small spike in `gpu-a100-2` too. error rate still low but p99 is creeping.
infra-bot: ALERT: high_queue_length detected in northstar (avg_queue=1720, p99_lat=1.8s)
raj: is this network-induced fan-in or a load test? any client-side retry storms?
sasha: CDN failover -> fan-in, no known test. a few big customers (enterprise) have heavy batched requests.
dan-oncall: we need to avoid hard rejects for enterprise SLA customers. can we do a soft-degrade first?
maria: proposal: try a "backfill-degrade" mode: accept short/light requests from new sessions and backfill capacity by preempting queued long batches, and rate-limit long-running requests. basically prefer many small responses over few huge ones.
lee: tradeoffs: reduces tail latency for small requests but costs could spike if we run more concurrent small inferences. also risk of starvation for high-cost jobs.
raj: alternative is longer queue + strict max-queue-ms which preserves order but increases p99 latency. we could also do probabilistic rejects for low-priority tokens.
sasha: head-of-line blocking is my main worry — if a few huge batches sit at the front we stall everyone. backfill helps.
dan-oncall: ok but how do we ensure enterprise customers get their commits? we should mark certain tokens as "protected" and never preempt them. can we do that with current admit controller?
maria: yes, we have a priority tag on tokens. protected requests will be honored up to X capacity, then backfill runs only on untagged traffic.
raj: quick config sketch: ```yaml
admit:
  strategy: backfill-degrade
  protect_priority: [enterprise, reserved]
  max_queue_ms: 2000
  long_request_token_limit: 1024
  probabilistic_reject_pct: 5  # for untagged heavy requests
```
lee: also add metrics we need to watch: queue_length, preempt_count, p50/p95/p99 latency, preempted_request_pct, enterprise_failures. set alert if enterprise_failures > 0.5% in 5m.
sasha: rollout plan: 1) enable backfill-degrade in canary AZ (northstar-a) for 10m 2) monitor metrics 3) if stable, expand to rest of northstar for 30m 4) enable probabilistic_reject at 5% then tune.
dan-oncall: who will push the config? I can if you give me the curl. i'll be oncall for next 60m.
maria: command to apply canary: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/regions/northstar/patch -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS' -d '{"admit_strategy":"backfill-degrade","max_queue_ms":2000,"probabilistic_reject_pct":5}'`
lee: also consider temporarily routing non-critical customers to fallback model (cheaper) — reduces GPU load quickly. ops route table easy to flip.
raj: cost note: backfill tends to increase small-request throughput so token-cost/unit might go up ~8-12% short-term. but avoids SLA violations which cost more.
sasha: agree. let's do canary. i'll watch head-of-line and preempt metrics.
infra-bot: ACTION: patch requested by maria. will apply to northstar-a canary after approval.
dan-oncall: approved. applying now.
infra-bot: CONFIG-UPDATE: northstar-a admit.strategy=backfill-degrade, max_queue_ms=2000, probabilistic_reject_pct=5 (applied by dan-oncall)
maria: seeing immediate drop in queue length in northstar-a from 1850 -> 420 within 90s. p50 latency for small requests down 30%.
lee: great. keep watch on enterprise failures and cost. set an alert if preempted_request_pct > 10% or enterprise_failures > 0.5%.
dan-oncall: noted. i'll hold on further rollout until eod or green from monitoring. thanks team. :thumbsup:
